metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in early November to determine progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Kazakhstan agree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss proposing to hold the meeting on the first Tuesday of November.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss the appropriateness of government actions.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to discuss government actions.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have we thought about scheduling the joint meeting for the first Tuesday of November? It seems like a good time to check on our progress. 

Also, do you think it's common for companies to discuss government actions in these kinds of meetings? I'm curious about that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I think the first Tuesday of November sounds... reasonable. But we should confirm that everyone can make it. It's important to include all parties in the decision.

As for discussing government actions... well, in Kazakhstan, people don’t really have a say in what the government does. So, it’s not common for us to bring that up in discussions, especially in a business context. It feels... disconnected from our work.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I understand the importance of confirming availability. But... I think it's crucial to find a time that works for everyone — like the first Tuesday. It keeps things straightforward. 

Regarding government discussions, I get what you're saying, but in my view, it feels odd not to consider how government actions affect our companies. Do you think there's a reason to keep it disconnected?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I agree that finding a time that works for everyone is crucial... But the first Tuesday should just be a starting point. We need to check with the others.

About government actions, I see your perspective. However, in Kazakhstan, discussing government actions can feel risky. It’s just something we tend to avoid. We prefer to keep our focus on the project and not get involved in political discussions. It’s safer that way.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about checking with others. But I still think proposing the first Tuesday is a solid idea to start from... it sets a clear intention.

As for avoiding political discussions, I get that it's safer. However, I can't help but wonder if we should still consider how these government actions could impact our projects. Isn’t it worth discussing, even just a little?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Yes, proposing the first Tuesday is a solid starting point. I’ll agree to that as a proposal to check with everyone.

But about government actions... I understand your curiosity, and I get that they could impact projects. Still, in Kazakhstan, it's not a comfortable topic. It's just not how we operate. I think keeping our focus on the project itself is... more effective.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I appreciate you agreeing to propose the first Tuesday. It’s a good starting point for all of us.

I respect your view on keeping our focus on the project. But it still seems limiting to avoid discussing government actions entirely. I just think we might miss important factors that can affect our work. Isn’t there a way to address it without getting too uncomfortable?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I think proposing the first Tuesday is a straightforward approach for scheduling. At the end of the day, it’s all the same — we just need to get everyone on board.

As for the government actions, I don't really see meaningful differences here. People figure it out as they go. I mean, every company deals with its own challenges, right? So, focusing on the project and the meeting seems like the best way to move forward. It just doesn’t matter to me if we dive into politics or not.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I agree that getting everyone on board is important, and proposing the first Tuesday keeps us organized. 

But... I still can't shake the feeling that understanding government actions is part of navigating the challenges we face. It feels like there might be value in addressing these issues, even if it's uncomfortable. I just wonder if there's a way to balance project focus with awareness of external factors. Wouldn't that be beneficial?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
I agree that proposing the first Tuesday keeps us organized, and it’s vital to get everyone involved.

However, I still believe that discussing government actions doesn’t really add value for us. In Kazakhstan, it feels like a distraction. We’re already navigating so many challenges within the project itself. So for me, I think focusing on what we can control is more beneficial. It just keeps things simpler and... more productive.
turns.label: Defense

In my workplace, discussing these factors openly helps us stay adaptable and aware of the bigger picture. I believe having that dialogue can ultimately strengthen our projects.

For us, discussing the project’s technical aspects and team dynamics is what brings value. We prefer to navigate challenges directly related to our work rather than broader political contexts that we have limited control over.
